parts.visual:
When a company wants to grow massively, the CEO must choose a direction: Up/Down or Sideways.

1. Vertical Integration: Buying the companies that supply your materials, or buying the stores that sell your product. You control the entire pipeline.
2. Horizontal Integration: Buying your direct competitors. You eliminate the competition and dominate a single step of the supply chain.
parts.audio: To grow massively, executives choose Vertical or Horizontal Integration. Vertical integration means buying your suppliers. Horizontal integration means buying your direct competitors.

questions.question: A massive coffee shop chain decides to buy a farm in Colombia that grows coffee beans, and a factory that roasts them. What is this?
options: Vertical Integration (Backward). They are moving backward down their supply chain to own the raw materials.
questions.correct_answer: Vertical Integration (Backward). They are moving backward down their supply chain to own the raw materials.
questions.explanation: By owning the farm, the coffee shop guarantees their supply and lowers their material costs.

questions.question: Listen to the CEO. What type of growth strategy is this?
questions.tts_text: We are the second largest ride-sharing app in the country. I want to buy the third largest ride-sharing app to eliminate them and steal their users.
questions.explanation: Buying a competitor who does the exact same thing as you is Horizontal Integration. It increases market share rapidly.

questions.question: Why does the government hate 'Horizontal Integration' much more than Vertical Integration?
options: Because Horizontal Integration directly eliminates competition. If you buy all your competitors, you create a monopoly, which triggers Anti-Trust lawsuits.
questions.correct_answer: Because Horizontal Integration directly eliminates competition. If you buy all your competitors, you create a monopoly, which triggers Anti-Trust lawsuits.
questions.explanation: The DOJ will rarely block a coffee shop from buying a farm, but they will aggressively block a phone company from buying another phone company.

questions.question: What is the primary risk of extreme Vertical Integration?
options: Loss of Focus. A software company that tries to build its own physical servers might fail because building hardware requires a completely different skill set.
questions.correct_answer: Loss of Focus. A software company that tries to build its own physical servers might fail because building hardware requires a completely different skill set.
questions.explanation: Doing one thing perfectly is easier than doing five things adequately.
